title: Code for: Can Scene-Level NWP Cloud Cover Replace Expert Pixel Labels? A Large-Scale Assessment with ERA5, GFS and CloudSEN12+
description:
Analysis and experiment code accompanying the manuscript Can Scene-Level NWP Cloud Cover Replace Expert Pixel Labels? A Large-Scale Assessment with ERA5, GFS and CloudSEN12+ by Anna Anzalone and Antonio Pagliaro, submitted to Applied Sciences (MDPI), 2026.

The study asks whether freely available cloud-cover fields from numerical weather prediction (NWP) products can replace expensive expert pixel-level annotations when training cloud detectors for Sentinel-2. It has two parts: the collocation of ERA5 and GFS total cloud cover with 48,380 expert-annotated CloudSEN12+ patches spanning 2017-2022, and a set of controlled U-Net experiments on the official region-disjoint partition of the dataset, evaluated on 975 held-out expert-annotated patches, in which only the source of the training labels varies.

The repository contains the download scripts for CloudSEN12+, ERA5 and GFS, the collocation and bootstrap statistics, the grouped bootstrap, the measurement of the ERA5 temporal offset, the collocation-scheme sensitivity test, and the U-Net training, evaluation and plotting scripts, together with a README mapping each script to the table or figure of the paper it produces. It also contains the collocation tables and the per-seed results of all 56 training runs.

Version 2.0.0 corresponds to the revised manuscript.
